title: Meeting Rooms II
prompt:
Given meeting time `intervals` (`[start, end]`), return the minimum number of conference rooms required so that no two overlapping meetings share a room. A meeting ending at time `t` frees its room for one starting at `t`.

**Example**: `[[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]]` → `2`.

**Constraints**: `0 ≤ intervals.length ≤ 10^4`.
hints: Go through meetings in start order. When a meeting begins, what do you need to know about the rooms already in use?
Only whether the soonest-ending ongoing meeting is finished. If it is, reuse its room. A min-heap of end times gives you that meeting in O(log n).
`if (!pq.isEmpty() && pq.peek() <= it[0]) pq.poll(); pq.offer(it[1]);`. The final heap size is the answer.

solution.explanation: In start order, the heap holds the end times of rooms in use. If the earliest end is ≤ the new start, that room is free and reused. Otherwise no room is free and a new one is needed. The heap only grows when every room is busy, so its size is the peak overlap. O(n log n) time, O(n) space. (Alternative: sort starts and ends separately and sweep with two pointers.)
